title: Safe Exploration via Policy Priors
claim: Starting from a conservative prior, exploring while safely falling back lets the set of safe policies expand toward the optimum.
layout: 3 regions: top robot-trajectory scene, bottom two blob diagrams, left-to-right; math above
description: The top panel is a real-world scene. An RC car at the lower left drives toward a crossed marker at the upper right, with tires as obstacles in the middle. A purple curve shows the final policy's return. A teal curve shows the iteration-n policy, which heads toward the tires. At a marked state s_t the agent switches to a black fallback path, the prior policy. A safety-criterion inequality in teal and purple sits above the scene. The bottom has two schematic panels, 'Exploration' and 'Expansion'. Each shows a green blob of policies that satisfy the constraint, with nested purple regions marking the policy sets Π^0 and Π^N. Dots mark π0, πN and the optimal policy π_c*. Purple arrows on the dashed boundary show the safe set growing outward. The eye goes first to the robot scene.
caption: We denote the implicit set of safe policies in iteration n by Πn
abstract: Safe exploration is a key requirement for reinforcement learning (RL) agents to learn and adapt online, beyond controlled (e.g. simulated) environments. In this work, we tackle this challenge by utilizing suboptimal yet conservative policies (e.g., obtained from offline data or simulators) as priors. Our approach, SOOPER, uses probabilistic dynamics models to optimistically explore, yet pessimistically fall back to the conservative policy prior if needed. We prove that SOOPER guarantees safety throughout learning, and establish convergence to an optimal policy by bounding its cumulative regret. Extensive experiments on key safe RL benchmarks and real-world hardware demonstrate that SOOPER is scalable, outperforms the state-of-the-art and validate our theoretical guarantees in practice.
